name: Seagate Exos X16 16TB
notes: ST16000NM001G. End-of-line; mostly sold as manufacturer-recertified now (~$230-260 recert). Still a solid $/TB anchor for 16TB.

name: Seagate Exos X18 16TB
notes: ST16000NM000J. Amazon marketplace listing ~$711 on 2026-09-06 (diskdojo); Newegg/SPD well under that. 18TB sibling ST18000NM000J ~$540.

name: Seagate Exos X20 20TB
notes: ST20000NM007D. SPD listed new at $500 but out of stock on 2026-09-06; Amazon $849, Newegg $880 same day. Recert ~$500. Loud under load; enterprise workhorse.

name: Seagate Exos X22 22TB
notes: ST22000NM001E. 512MB cache. Used/recert listings ~$29/TB (DatacenterDisk, Sept 2026).

name: Seagate Exos X24 24TB
notes: ST24000NM002H. Last conventional-PMR Exos before HAMR. Renewed units $620 (diskdojo 2026-09-06). Also sold in 12/16/20TB X24 SKUs.

name: Seagate Exos M 30TB (Mozaic 3+)
notes: ST30000NM004K. HAMR / Mozaic 3+ platform - first mass-market HAMR drive. 32TB SKU ~$1,900 on Amazon (inflated). Long-term HAMR reliability data still thin.

name: WD Ultrastar DC HC550 16TB
notes: WUH721816ALE6L4. Amazon $754 on 2026-09-06 (diskdojo). Same platform lives inside many WD Elements shuckables (white-label).

name: WD Ultrastar DC HC560 20TB
notes: WUH722020ALE6L4. Recert $599 at ServerPartDeals 2026-09-06 (60 in stock) - recert premium vs Seagate is unusual this year.

name: WD Ultrastar DC HC570 22TB
notes: WUH722222ALE6L4. Believed to be the drive inside 20/22TB WD Elements with reduced-speed firmware.

name: WD Ultrastar DC HC580 24TB
notes: WUH722424ALE6L4. Retail swung $679-$1,118 in Aug 2026 alone; Newegg is the sane price. Renewed ~$430 ($17.92/TB, DatacenterDisk).

name: WD Ultrastar DC HC590 26TB
notes: WUH722626ALE6L4. ePMR + OptiNAND; 11-platter. 24TB SKU was $469.99 in late 2025. Top of WD's conventional line before HAMR.

name: Toshiba MG09 18TB
notes: MG09ACA18TE. 9-platter helium; low idle power for its class. Amazon $659 on 2026-09-06. Used listings ~$35/TB.

name: Toshiba MG10 20TB
notes: MG10ACA20TE. FC-MAMR, 10-platter helium. Often the cheapest new 20TB from a US retailer; MG10F 22TB sibling. Recert/refurb ~$380 at SPD.

name: Toshiba MG11 24TB
notes: MG11ACA24TE. 1GB cache, MAMR. 22TB sibling $695 on Amazon 2026-09-06 ($31.58/TB) vs $1,096 Newegg - retailer spread is huge right now.

name: WD Red Plus 4TB
notes: WD40EFPX. All Red Plus are CMR (the SMR ones were rebranded plain 'WD Red' after the 2020 scandal - avoid WD40EFAX).

name: WD Red Plus 8TB
notes: WD80EFPX. 2026 price whiplash: $180 in May, $355 by Jul-Sep. Used ~$215. Quiet, cool; 3-yr warranty is the weak spot vs Pro.

name: WD Red Plus 12TB
notes: WD120EFBX. 12TB+ Red Plus are helium 7200 class despite the 'Plus' badge.

name: WD Red Pro 16TB
notes: WD161KFGX. Essentially an Ultrastar with NAS firmware and a 5-yr warranty; you pay ~$100-150 over HC550 for the badge.

name: WD Red Pro 22TB
notes: WD221KFGX. OptiNAND. 24TB $1,000 and 26TB $1,145 on the same day - little $/TB advantage at the top.

name: Seagate IronWolf 4TB
notes: ST4000VN006. All IronWolf are CMR. Includes 3 yrs Rescue data recovery.

name: Seagate IronWolf 8TB
notes: ST8000VN004 / ST8000VNZ04. 7200 rpm air drive - hotter and louder than Red Plus 8TB, and now priced about the same.

name: Seagate IronWolf Pro 16TB
notes: ST16000NT001. Exos X18 platform with NAS firmware + 3 yr Rescue. Newegg had OEM units at $265 in Sept 2025.

name: Seagate IronWolf Pro 24TB
notes: ST24000NT002. Exos X24 platform. 22TB sibling $895 on Amazon 2026-09-06 (diskdojo) - 24TB is the better buy.

name: Seagate IronWolf Pro 30TB (Mozaic 3+)
notes: ST30000NT011. HAMR for NAS. 28TB was $479.99 at Best Buy Oct 2025 ($17/TB) - that price is gone.

name: Toshiba N300 8TB
notes: HDWG480. All N300 are CMR. 7200 rpm air drive; Toshiba's NAS drives are consistently cheaper than WD/Seagate equivalents when in stock.

name: Toshiba N300 Pro 16TB
notes: HDWG51GXZSTB. MG09 platform. Rated 300 TB/yr (not 550) - Toshiba's Pro is 'up to 24 bays', a notch below Red Pro/IronWolf Pro.

name: Toshiba N300 Pro 20TB
notes: HDWG62AXZSTB. MG10 platform. Tracked range $379 (Dec 2025) to $1,048 (May 2026) - most volatile line in this dataset.

name: WD Purple 4TB
notes: WD43PURZ. AllFrame AI firmware, up to 64 cameras. Same mechanics as Red Plus 4TB; buy whichever is cheaper.

name: WD Purple 8TB
notes: WD85PURZ. Top of the non-Pro Purple line; above 8TB you must go Purple Pro.

name: WD Purple Pro 12TB
notes: WD122PURP (older WD121PURP has 256MB). Best Buy $299.99 in Sept 2026 makes this an odd bargain: an Ultrastar-class helium drive cheaper per TB than Red Pro.

name: WD Purple Pro 18TB
notes: WD181PURP. 550 TB/yr, 2.5M MTBF - enterprise spec with surveillance firmware; fine in a NAS.

name: Seagate SkyHawk 4TB
notes: ST4000VX016. Current-gen SkyHawk 2-8TB (VX017/VX016/VX009/VX010) are SMR per Seagate's product manual - fine for sequential DVR writes, bad for NAS/RAID.

name: Seagate SkyHawk 8TB
notes: ST8000VX010. SMR (the older ST8000VX0022 was CMR - watch the model number). Do not use in RAID/ZFS.

name: Seagate SkyHawk AI 12TB
notes: ST12000VE001. Exos-based helium CMR, 550 TB/yr, 3 yr Rescue. Like Purple Pro, often priced below the NAS-branded equivalent.

name: Seagate SkyHawk AI 20TB
notes: ST20000VE002. Exos X20 platform.

name: WD Blue 4TB (WD40EZAX)
notes: CMR. The sneaky sibling WD40EZAZ (same name, same shelf) is SMR - check the last letter. 2-yr warranty. Workload rating is WD's 55 TB/yr consumer figure.

name: WD Blue 8TB (WD80EAAZ)
notes: CMR, helium-free 5640 rpm. Cheapest CMR 8TB most months; effectively a Red Plus 8TB with a 2-yr warranty.

name: Seagate BarraCuda 4TB (3.5")
notes: ST4000DM004. Every 3.5" BarraCuda 2TB+ is drive-managed SMR. Fine as a bulk media drive; miserable for RAID rebuilds or random writes.

name: Seagate BarraCuda 8TB (3.5")
notes: ST8000DM004. SMR. Note: 20-24TB 'BarraCuda' (ST24000DM001) is a different, CMR Exos-derived drive found in Expansion externals.

name: Toshiba P300 4TB
notes: HDWD240. 4TB and 6TB P300 are 5400 rpm SMR; 1-3TB P300 are 7200 rpm CMR.

name: Toshiba P300 3TB
notes: HDWD130. Last CMR 7200 rpm desktop drive in Toshiba's consumer line; 64MB cache.

name: WD Elements Desktop 20TB
notes: WDBWLG0200HBK. Shucks to a white-label Ultrastar (HC550/HC570 class, WD200EDGZ) with speed-limited firmware; may need the 3.3V pin tape trick. 2-yr warranty; WD generally honors by serial. Best $/TB new-in-box play in 2026.

name: WD My Book 22TB
notes: WDBBGB0220HBK. Same internals as Elements but 3-yr warranty and hardware encryption in the bridge (irrelevant once shucked).

name: Seagate Expansion Desktop 16TB
notes: STKP16000400. Shucks to a BarraCuda-labelled Exos (ST16000DM001-class). 2-yr warranty (some regions 1-yr).

name: Seagate Expansion Desktop 24TB
notes: STKP24000400. Contains ST24000DM001 (Exos X24 mechanics). Was $240 ($10/TB) in Nov 2025 - nearly doubled since. Still the cheapest way to buy a 24TB CMR drive.

name: Seagate Expansion Desktop 28TB
notes: STKP28000400. Believed to contain a HAMR (Mozaic 3+) BarraCuda-labelled Exos M - first shuckable HAMR drive; long-term data thin.

name: Seagate BarraCuda 2TB (2.5")
notes: ST2000LM015, 7mm. SMR (all 2.5" BarraCuda 1TB+ are). The 5TB ST5000LM000 is 15mm thick and won't fit most laptops.

name: Seagate BarraCuda 5TB (2.5")
notes: ST5000LM000, 15mm z-height. SMR. Highest capacity 2.5" HDD you can buy; same drive lives in Seagate 5TB portables.

name: WD Blue Mobile 2TB
notes: WD20SPZX, 7mm. SMR. 1TB WD10SPZX is also SMR; only the old 9.5mm WD10JPVX is CMR.

name: Toshiba L200 2TB
notes: HDWL120, 9.5mm. SMR. The 1TB HDWL110 (7mm) is CMR - the only current CMR 2.5" consumer HDD.
